newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 32 to 913 in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 32 to 913 in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 913 as of Friday, up 32 from the prior week and 141 above the year-ago total of 772, Baker Hughes Inc. said.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by 37 to 769, while rigs working offshore dropped by four to 119.

The number of rigs active in inland waters fell by one to 25. Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which rose by nine, Louisiana and Wyoming, which both rose by five and California, which rose by two.
Rigs in the Gulf of Mexico dipped five to 113.
A total of 374 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up five from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 27 to 535, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at four.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 32 to 207, vs. 78 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 170 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of May 9, up one from the period ending May 2.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 180, was 94.4 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area was up two at 105 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 106, a utilization rate of 99.1 pct.
The worldwide rig count was up two at 576 out of a total fleet of 603, with a utilization rate of 95.5 percent.
